risk_order.label: Firm-fixed-price (FFP)
risk_order.why: One price no matter what it costs the contractor: the contractor carries all the cost risk.

risk_order.label: Fixed-price with economic price adjustment (FP-EPA)
risk_order.why: Still fixed price, but named market changes such as fuel or steel prices move the price.

risk_order.label: Fixed-price incentive (FPIF)
risk_order.why: Costs above target are shared, up to a ceiling price; the contractor still carries risk above the ceiling.

risk_order.label: Cost-plus-incentive-fee (CPIF)
risk_order.why: The Government pays allowable costs; the fee shrinks if costs run high, so the contractor shares a little risk.

risk_order.label: Cost-plus-award-fee (CPAF)
risk_order.why: The Government pays allowable costs; the fee depends on a subjective performance rating.

risk_order.label: Cost-plus-fixed-fee (CPFF)
risk_order.why: The Government pays allowable costs plus a set fee; the contractor's profit does not drop when costs rise.

risk_order.label: Time-and-materials (T&M)
risk_order.why: The Government pays for every hour used plus materials: no profit incentive to control hours, so the Government watches closely.

phase_sort.task: Holding a post-award orientation conference with the new contractor
phase_sort.why: It happens after award to start administration off right.

phase_sort.task: Deciding whether to set a requirement aside for small business
phase_sort.why: Set-aside decisions are part of the acquisition strategy before the solicitation.

phase_sort.task: Comparing three quotes to decide whether a price is fair and reasonable
phase_sort.why: Price analysis is an Award competency (Price or Cost Analysis).

phase_sort.task: Writing a performance work statement with the customer
phase_sort.why: Describing the requirement is the first Pre-Award job task.

phase_sort.task: Deobligating leftover funds and closing the contract file
phase_sort.why: That is closeout, the last part of Post-Award.

phase_sort.task: Refusing a gift from a contractor during an open competition
phase_sort.why: Standards of conduct apply in every phase: a Guiding Principle.

phase_sort.task: Responding to a GAO protest of an award
phase_sort.why: Managing protests is the Award competency Manage Disagreements.

phase_sort.task: Issuing a change order for additional work within scope
phase_sort.why: Changes are managed after award (Manage Changes).

phase_sort.task: Posting a sources sought notice on SAM.gov
phase_sort.why: Sources sought notices are market research before the solicitation.

phase_sort.task: Setting prenegotiation objectives before talks with an offeror
phase_sort.why: Planning negotiations is an Award competency.

phase_sort.task: Explaining to a commander that only a contracting officer can sign a contract
phase_sort.why: Authority is a Contract Principle that applies everywhere.

phase_sort.task: Reviewing a prime's request for consent to subcontract
phase_sort.why: Managing subcontracts happens during performance.

phase_sort.task: Answering offerors' questions and issuing a solicitation amendment
phase_sort.why: Request Offers covers releasing and amending the solicitation.

phase_sort.task: Debriefing an unsuccessful offeror
phase_sort.why: Debriefings are part of finalizing the award (Select Source).

phase_sort.task: Inspecting delivered items and signing the receiving report
phase_sort.why: Inspection and acceptance are Ensure Quality tasks after award.

phase_sort.task: Writing a memo for record so the file explains a decision
phase_sort.why: Communication and documentation is a Guiding Principle used in every phase.

phase_sort.task: Choosing between firm-fixed-price and cost-reimbursement
phase_sort.why: Contract type is part of the strategy before solicitation.

phase_sort.task: Making the source selection decision and documenting the tradeoff
phase_sort.why: Select Source is an Award competency.

phase_sort.task: Writing the final CPARS evaluation
phase_sort.why: Final performance evaluations are part of closeout.

phase_sort.task: Working as a team with the customer, legal and finance
phase_sort.why: Team dynamics is a Guiding Principle.

phase_sort.task: Determining a prospective contractor is responsible
phase_sort.why: Responsibility is decided before award, as part of selecting the source.

phase_sort.task: Sending a cure notice for poor performance
phase_sort.why: Cure notices come during performance, before a possible termination.

phase_sort.task: Preparing the IGCE with the requiring activity
phase_sort.why: The IGCE is built while planning the solicitation.

phase_sort.task: A company deciding whether to bid on a solicitation
phase_sort.why: Plan Sales is the seller's Pre-Award task.

phase_sort.task: Issuing a final decision on a contractor's claim
phase_sort.why: Claims are resolved under Manage Changes, after award.

phase_sort.task: Reporting a suspected kickback to legal counsel
phase_sort.why: Standards of conduct apply in every phase.

phase_sort.task: Establishing the competitive range
phase_sort.why: The competitive range is set during evaluation before award.

phase_sort.task: Exercising an option for another year of service
phase_sort.why: Options are exercised during administration of an awarded contract.

threshold.scenario: A $9,800 commercial buy of office supplies, no contingency.
threshold.answer: Micro-purchase: no competitive quotes needed if the price is reasonable
choices: Micro-purchase: no competitive quotes needed if the price is reasonable
Simplified procedures with at least three quotes
Full FAR Part 15 source selection
Certified cost or pricing data required
threshold.why: $9,800 is at or below the $15,000 micro-purchase threshold.

threshold.scenario: A $14,500 purchase of commercial tools, no contingency.
threshold.answer: Micro-purchase: no competitive quotes needed if the price is reasonable
choices: Micro-purchase: no competitive quotes needed if the price is reasonable
Simplified procedures with at least three quotes
Sealed bidding
A justification is required
threshold.why: $14,500 is still at or below the $15,000 micro-purchase threshold.

threshold.scenario: A $120,000 commercial furniture buy in the United States.
threshold.answer: Simplified procedures (FAR 12.201-1), quotes from at least three sources when practicable
choices: Simplified procedures (FAR 12.201-1), quotes from at least three sources when practicable
Micro-purchase with the purchase card
Certified cost or pricing data required
FAR Part 13 noncommercial procedures
threshold.why: Above the MPT and at or below the SAT; commercial simplified buys follow Part 12 under the RFO.

threshold.answer: FAR Part 13 simplified procedures for noncommercial items
choices: FAR Part 13 simplified procedures for noncommercial items
FAR 12.201-1 commercial procedures
Micro-purchase
Certified cost or pricing data required
threshold.why: Noncommercial and at or below the $350,000 SAT, so Part 13 applies.

threshold.scenario: A $2.4 million commercial buy of laptops.
threshold.answer: Commercial simplified procedures can still be used (up to $9 million)
choices: Commercial simplified procedures can still be used (up to $9 million)
It must use FAR Part 15 because it is over the SAT
Micro-purchase
Certified cost or pricing data required
threshold.why: Under the RFO, simplified procedures for commercial items go up to $9 million.

threshold.scenario: A $12 million commercial services buy, no contingency.
threshold.answer: Above the $9 million commercial simplified ceiling: use other procedures, often Part 15
choices: Above the $9 million commercial simplified ceiling: use other procedures, often Part 15
Micro-purchase
Simplified procedures up to the SAT
Certified cost or pricing data always required
threshold.why: Commercial simplified procedures stop at $9 million ($15 million only with a contingency determination).

threshold.scenario: A $22,000 noncommercial buy. Do you need to post a presolicitation notice?
threshold.answer: Yes: above $20,000 a notice is required unless an exemption applies (posted 10 days for $20,000 to $25,000)
choices: Yes: above $20,000 a notice is required unless an exemption applies (posted 10 days for $20,000 to $25,000)
No: notices start at $25,000
No: notices start at the SAT
Only if the buy is commercial
threshold.why: The RFO FAR lowered the notice trigger to above $20,000.

threshold.scenario: During a declared contingency overseas (with the determination), a $35,000 buy of generators.
threshold.answer: Micro-purchase: the contingency threshold outside the U.S. is $40,000
choices: Micro-purchase: the contingency threshold outside the U.S. is $40,000
Simplified procedures with three quotes because it is over $15,000
Sealed bidding
A J&A is required
threshold.why: With the determination, the micro-purchase threshold outside the U.S. is $40,000.

threshold.scenario: During a domestic emergency (with the determination), a $30,000 buy of water.
threshold.answer: Simplified procedures: the contingency micro-purchase threshold inside the U.S. is only $25,000
choices: Simplified procedures: the contingency micro-purchase threshold inside the U.S. is only $25,000
Micro-purchase, because the outside-U.S. figure is $40,000
Certified cost or pricing data required
No rules apply in an emergency
threshold.why: Inside the U.S. the contingency MPT is $25,000, so $30,000 is above it.

threshold.scenario: A DoW sole-source contract for $6 million, awarded in November 2026, noncommercial, no exception applies.
threshold.answer: Certified cost or pricing data are NOT required: DoW's threshold is $10 million for awards after 30 June 2026
choices: Certified cost or pricing data are NOT required: DoW's threshold is $10 million for awards after 30 June 2026
Certified cost or pricing data are required because it is over $2.5 million
Certified cost or pricing data are never allowed
A GAO review is required
threshold.why: For DoW awards after 30 June 2026 the threshold is $10 million (FY2026 NDAA; DFARS 215.403-3 deviation). You may still ask for other data you need.

threshold.scenario: A DoW sole-source contract for $14 million, awarded in December 2026, noncommercial, no exception applies.
threshold.answer: Certified cost or pricing data are required
choices: Certified cost or pricing data are required
Not required, because it is a sole source
Not required above $10 million
Only an IGCE is needed
threshold.why: $14 million is above DoW's $10 million threshold and no exception applies.

threshold.scenario: A DoW justification for other than full and open competition worth $8 million. Who approves it?
threshold.answer: The contracting officer (by certifying the justification)
choices: The contracting officer (by certifying the justification)
The competition advocate
The head of the contracting activity
The senior procurement executive
threshold.why: DoW's Table 206-1 sets $10 million or below at the contracting officer level.

threshold.scenario: A DoW justification worth $60 million. Who approves it?
choices: The competition advocate
The contracting officer
The head of the contracting activity
The senior procurement executive
threshold.why: Over $10 million up to $100 million goes to the competition advocate in DoW.

threshold.scenario: A DoW justification worth $250 million. Who approves it?
threshold.answer: The head of the contracting activity
choices: The head of the contracting activity
The competition advocate
The contracting officer
The senior procurement executive
threshold.why: Over $100 million up to $500 million goes to the HCA in DoW.

threshold.scenario: A contractor submits a $75,000 claim. Must it be certified?
threshold.answer: No: certification is required only for claims over $100,000
choices: No: certification is required only for claims over $100,000
Yes: every claim must be certified
Yes: claims over $50,000 must be certified
Only if it is a Government claim
threshold.why: The Contract Disputes Act requires certification above $100,000.

threshold.scenario: A protest of a $28 million DoW task order that does not change the contract's scope, period or maximum value. Can GAO hear it?
threshold.answer: No: for DoW orders, GAO's floor is above $35 million
choices: No: for DoW orders, GAO's floor is above $35 million
Yes: GAO hears all order protests
Yes: the floor is $10 million
Only at the Court of Federal Claims
threshold.why: The FY2025 NDAA set DoW's order-protest floor at $35 million.
